text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
NASA BORBA
- Serbian government recognises opposition coalition win in Serbia's southern town of Nis and instructs justice ministry to determine responsibility for irregularities in elections there.
- Opposition coalition supporters demonstrate in Belgrade, blocking streets with their cars. Police beat demonstrators in one part of town.
- Opposition protests continue in other parts of Serbia -- Nis, Kragujevac, Cuprija, Sabac, Valjevo.
- Constituent session of the Vojvodina province assembly will be held in Novi Sad on Thursday.
- Yugoslav United Left (JUL) urges all embassies to condemn opposition coalition Zajedno for terrorism, calls for violence and spreading intolerance.
- Tradesmen increase prices of domestic and foreign goods 10 to 20 percent to cover last week's fall of dinar on currency black market.
- Black market dinar exchange rate stabilises in most towns at 4.5 dinars for the German mark (official rate 3.3 dinars).
POLITIKA
- There will be no devaluation of dinar. Citizens can buy up to 1,000 German marks in banks at official exchange rate (3.3 dinars for one mark), paper learns from its sources.
- Slavija bank expects decision on its closure to be revoked, bank said in staatement.
- central bank of Yugoslavia Board of Governors to hold regular meeting Friday. Bankers do not expect any spectacular decisions or devaluation of the dinar.
- New Yugoslavia citizenship law took effect January 1.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Exit tax for Yugoslav citizens will remain in effect in 1997, says federal government.

- Workers of the company of department stores Beograd continue strike for 22nd day. Strikers' negotiating team decides at meeting with Serbian Trade Minister Srdjan Nikolic to call an emergency meeting of the company's managing board.
- Bosnian Serb republic celebrates Republic Day in the northern town of Brcko Thursday.
BORBA
- Serbia's new amended sales tax law introduces five percent excise duty for table salt. Duties imposed on oil, tobacco, coffee, alcoholic beverages.
